research_summary.scope: Painting pre-primed interior trim (baseboard, door casing, window casing) in new construction. All trim same color and sheen. Full prep per Fine Finish Doctrine.
research_summary.substrate: Pre-primed MDF, finger-joint pine, or solid wood trim
research_summary.condition_assumption: Factory-primed trim with variable installation quality - condition class determines prep intensity
key_findings: Pre-primed trim has 2 fastener holes (stacked vertically) every 12-16 inches from installation
Caulking required at all trim-to-wall and trim-to-trim joints
Open grain board ends may require filling with putty or caulk for uniform finish acceptance
Workflow follows Fine Finish Doctrine: Initial Prep → Finish Coat 1 → Interstage → Finish Coat 2
Interstage process runs after each coat EXCEPT final: Clean → Inspect → Light sand → Patch → Sand patches → Spot coat patches
Semi-gloss typical for trim (requires QT4 or higher per doctrine)
Satin acceptable at QT3; gloss requires QT5 per doctrine
Condition classification (Good/Fair/Poor) drives prep time estimation

fine_finish_workflow.description: NC trim painting follows Fine Finish Doctrine with Initial Prep and Interstage phases

tasks: TSK_FF_CLEAN_SURFACES_FLOORS - Protect floors and adjacent surfaces
TSK_FF_WIPE_DOWN_SURFACES - Remove dust from trim surfaces

sequence.description: Primary fill-sand-caulk cycle before first finish coat (primer optional on factory-primed)
tasks: TSK_FF_FILL_FASTENERS - Fill 2 stacked nail holes every 12-16 inches
TSK_FF_FILL_GAPS - Caulk or fill gaps at miters, wall intersections, open grain at board ends
TSK_FF_FULL_SAND - Sand entire surface for adhesion
TSK_FF_CLEAN_WORK_AREA - Clean floors, remove overspray accumulation
TSK_FF_INSPECT_COAT - Inspect for dust nibs, missed holes revealed by first coat
TSK_FF_LIGHT_SAND - Scuff sand full surface (220 grit)
TSK_FF_PATCH_REPAIR - Fill defects revealed by first coat
TSK_FF_SPOT_COAT_PATCHES - Brush-apply finish over patches to seal
sequence.notes: Interstage is lighter than Initial Prep - maintenance only

tasks: TSK_FF_FINAL_INSPECTION - Walk inspection per tier scrutiny level

fine_finish_workflow.interstage_run_rule: Interstage runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat

factory_primer.type: Typically alkyd or latex primer applied at factory
factory_primer.adhesion_notes: Factory primer generally has good adhesion; scuff sand recommended per Fine Finish Doctrine Initial Prep
factory_primer.primer_decision: Per doctrine: factory-primed = primer optional (user decision)

common_materials: MDF (medium-density fiberboard) - most common in production NC
Solid pine or poplar - higher-end NC
PVC/composite trim - requires specific primers if bare

open_grain_considerations.description: Open grain board ends visible at exposed casing end cuts on door and window openings
typical_locations: Door header casing ends (2 per door opening SIDE)
Window header casing ends (2 per window opening)
Window sill/lower casing ends (2 per window opening)

quantification.door_counting_note: Door openings counted per SIDE: interior door = 2 sides (2 casing sets), exterior door = 1 interior side (1 casing set)

open_grain_considerations.treatment: Fill with putty or caulk, wipe smooth before painting - separate task TSK_TRIM_FILL_OPEN_GRAIN
open_grain_considerations.cope_and_miter_joints: Cope cuts and miter joints on running trim generally overlap and are handled with caulk/putty during normal prep tasks
open_grain_considerations.failure_if_untreated: Open grain absorbs finish unevenly, causing visible texture differences at casing ends

fastener_pattern.standard_pattern: 2 fastener holes (one above the other, stacked vertically) every 12-16 inches
fastener_pattern.rationale: Top and bottom nailing secures trim to wall framing and prevents cupping
fastener_pattern.typical_density_per_lf: Approximately 1.5-2 hole pairs per linear foot

typical_defects: 2 stacked brad/finish nail holes every 12-16 inches
Gaps at miter joints (typical 1/32 to 1/8 inch)
Gaps between trim and wall surface
Open grain at cut ends on wood trim
variable_defects: Smudges and dirt from handling during installation
Excessive fastener holes from repositioning or mistakes
Large gaps at seams (poor carpentry or material warping)
Large gaps at wall interface (wall irregularities)

condition_classification.description: Trim condition at installation varies significantly. Gap size and defect density are difficult to measure individually. Use condition class as heuristic for prep time estimation.
condition_classification.classification_approach: Estimator assigns condition class based on overall assessment of all imperfections: fastener holes, gaps, damage, cleanliness, open grain treatment needed.

criteria: Standard fastener hole density (2 stacked holes every 12-16 inches)
Tight miter joints (1/32 inch or less)
Small gaps at wall (1/16 inch or less)
classes.notes: Standard NC quality - competent trim installation

criteria: Above-average fastener holes (repositioning evident, extra holes)
Visible gaps at miter joints (1/16 to 1/8 inch)
Moderate gaps at wall (1/8 to 1/4 inch)
Some handling damage requiring additional fill
Noticeable open grain at cuts requiring treatment
classes.notes: Below-average installation quality or material issues

criteria: Excessive fastener holes (multiple repositions, blown-out holes)
Large gaps at miter joints (1/8 inch or more)
Large gaps at wall (1/4 inch or more, may require multiple caulk passes)
Significant damage requiring substantial fill or replacement
Extensive open grain requiring fill treatment at all cuts
classes.notes: Poor installation quality - consider flagging for carpentry remediation or hourly billing on prep

condition_classification.estimator_guidance: Walk trim and assess holistically. If gaps and defects are notably worse than typical, upgrade condition class. When in doubt, document with photos and quote Fair condition.

quality_tier_behavior.principle: Quality tier controls scrutiny, not process steps. Same tasks exist at all tiers. Higher tiers execute with slower pace, tighter tolerances, more thorough inspection.

sheen_restrictions.QT3: Satin or lower (flat, matte, eggshell, satin)

inspection_depth.QT5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length

interstage_sanding.QT3: Spot sand only - address visible nibs, rough spots
interstage_sanding.QT4: Light full sand 220 grit - entire surface scuffed
interstage_sanding.QT5: Thorough full sand 220-320 grit - uniformly smooth to touch

modified_urethane_benefits: Alkyd-like flow and leveling (reduces brush marks)

application_methods.spray_masking_note: For spray application, all edges are masked - there is no cut-in with spray. Full masking required.

brush_roll_edge_strategy.QT3: Freehand cut-in acceptable; tape line optional
brush_roll_edge_strategy.QT4: Tape line recommended for cleaner edges
brush_roll_edge_strategy.QT5: Tape line with edge seal required for crisp lines

trim_to_wall.description: Trim edge meets painted or unpainted drywall
trim_to_wall.nc_typical: Walls not yet finished - no masking needed at trim-to-wall edge for spray
trim_to_wall.if_walls_finished: Full masking required per spray application

trim_to_floor.strategy: Quarter-round typically covers gap; floor protection during spray

casing_to_jamb.typical_scenario: Casing and jamb painted same color, sheen, and material - treated as single scope
casing_to_jamb.variant_stained_jamb: Jambs may be stained and cleared while casing is painted. Requires masking at casing-to-jamb interface.
casing_to_jamb.variant_different_color: Jambs may be painted different color than casing. Requires masking at interface.

required_paintscope_keys.purpose: Door opening count for open grain fill calculation (2 casing ends per opening SIDE). Counted per side: interior door = 2 sides, exterior door = 1 interior side.
Window opening count for open grain fill calculation (4 casing ends per opening)
Floor protection area if spray method

professional_practice_notes.prep_sequence: Setup → Initial Prep (fill holes, fill open grain, sand, clean dust, caulk) → Finish Coat 1 → Interstage (clean, inspect, sand, patch, spot coat) → Finish Coat 2 → Final Inspection
professional_practice_notes.typical_coat_system: Factory primer + 2 finish coats (no additional primer on factory-primed)
professional_practice_notes.interstage_purpose: First coat reveals hidden defects; interstage addresses them before final coat
professional_practice_notes.caulk_timing: Major caulking in Initial Prep before first finish coat
professional_practice_notes.open_grain_treatment: Apply putty or caulk to exposed casing ends at door/window openings (2 per door, 4 per window) - separate task TSK_TRIM_FILL_OPEN_GRAIN; cope cuts and miter joints handled during normal caulk tasks

sanding_grit.interstage_light_sand: 220 grit (QT3 spot only; QT4/QT5 full surface)

professional_practice_notes.nc_caulk_consumption: Approximately 72 LF per tube (per Materials doctrine)
professional_practice_notes.nc_spackle_consumption: Significantly higher than repaint (3-5x) due to overfill-and-sand method

doctrine_references.key_alignment: Trim follows Fine Finish Doctrine as linear element (LF-based)

sections: Spackle - Exception: New Construction Trim Fastener Filling
key_points: NC fastener fill has high waste factor (3-5x repaint)
